lines.trans: Joon-mo, honestly I regret it a lot—moving into your apartment and making a nuisance of myself.
And blurting out foolish things drunk and flustering you—I am sorry for all of it. I shook our twenty-five-year friendship.
Once I move out into my place, the two of us go right back to where we belong.
Ye-jin, suppose we each meet someone else and get married—and your husband and my wife dislike how close we are.
Honestly, would disliking it not be completely natural? How could we keep up a bond like this after marrying other people?
So once you get married, you plan to stop seeing me?
We work at the same station so of course we will see each other, yet things could never stay the way they are now.
Except I really do not like the sound of that.
Even if you hate it, what can you do? Is that not the natural limit of friendship between a man and a woman?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Yes, let's each head to our own separate homes, senior!
Here the word for 'each person's own' is key.

meanings.note: Used as bound noun (간).

examples.text: 싫으면 어쩔 건데? 이런 게 이성 간 우정의 한계 이런 거 아니겠냐!
examples.trans: Even if you hate it, what can you do? Is that not the natural limit of friendship between a man and a woman?

examples.text: 심지어 파일럿 프로그램이 그 시간대에 들어간다? 그건 까놓고 얘기해서 간 본다는 거거든!
examples.trans: Worse yet, slotting a pilot right into their broadcast hour? Frankly speaking, management is testing the waters!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (결혼을).

examples.text: 예진아, 우리가 각자 다른 남자 여자 만나서 결혼을 한다 치자. 근데 서로의 와이프 남편이 우리의 이런 관계를 싫어해.
examples.trans: Ye-jin, suppose we each meet someone else and get married—and your husband and my wife dislike how close we are.
This point about marriage is really important.

examples.text: 내가 전에 말했잖아, 준모 형이랑 결혼해서 우리 집 되찾으라고.
examples.trans: I told you before, marry Joon-mo and win back our family apartment.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 결혼하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (marry and).

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term for human or logical relations.

examples.trans: human relations
What is the relationship between those two?

meanings.en: to be bothersome, annoying, a hassle
meanings.note: Describes something troublesome or too much effort to deal with.

examples.trans: Cooking is a hassle.
It's a hassle if there are lots of people.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

meanings.note: Used as conjunction (그렇지만).

examples.text: 역시 우리 신디는 똑똑해. 그렇지만 신디야, 난 잃어봤단다.
examples.trans: Smart as ever, our Cindy—except Cindy, I have already lost a star like you once before.

examples.text: 너처럼 나한텐 소중한 아이였어. 그렇지만 그 아이를 잃고 나니까 네가 왔잖니?
examples.trans: She was just as precious to me as you are—yet right after I lost her, you came along, remember?
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (남편이).

examples.text: 예진아, 우리가 각자 다른 남자 여자 만나서 결혼을 한다 치자. 근데 서로의 와이프 남편이 우리의 이런 관계를 싫어해.
examples.trans: Ye-jin, suppose we each meet someone else and get married—and your husband and my wife dislike how close we are.
This point about and husband is really important.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Did you hear about this you guys?
I was busy today because of you guys.

examples.text: 나 십 년 동안 시키는 대로 다 했잖아요.
examples.trans: For ten years, I did everything you told me to do.

examples.text: 이십 년 넘게 친구 설정으로 지냈는데 쉽진 않겠지.
examples.trans: You lived as friends for over twenty years, so changing that won't be easy.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: 르-irregular adjective; conjugates as 달라요 in polite present.
In its adnominal form 다른, modifies a following noun to mean 'other' or 'another'.

examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?
Our thoughts are different from each other.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

examples.text: 당연해 그건. 점심 먹어야지. 여기서 군만두 맛있어.
examples.trans: Of course you won't. Let's eat lunch. The fried dumplings here are delicious.
Today's atmosphere is truly natural, of course.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (당황시킨).

examples.text: 그리고 내가 술 먹고 실언한 거, 너 당황시킨 거 다 미안해. 내가 흔들었어, 우리 25년 우정.
examples.trans: And blurting out foolish things drunk and flustering you—I am sorry for all of it. I shook our twenty-five-year friendship.
Let us do that (flustered) right away.
I want to works, spins right now.
How about trying to works, spins together tomorrow?
Please come into the room.

examples.text: 올해 우리 회사에 신입사원이 많이 들어왔어요.
examples.trans: Many new employees joined our company this year.

meanings.note: Compound of 들다 (enter) + 오다 (come)

meanings.en: to join (a company, school, or group)

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.en: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
meanings.note: adverbial use of the noun 사실 (fact)

examples.trans: Honestly, I don't know well either.
In fact, I couldn't sleep yesterday.

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

examples.text: 서로 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (each other), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (실언한).

examples.text: 그리고 내가 술 먹고 실언한 거, 너 당황시킨 거 다 미안해. 내가 흔들었어, 우리 25년 우정.
examples.trans: And blurting out foolish things drunk and flustering you—I am sorry for all of it. I shook our twenty-five-year friendship.
Let us do that (spoke out of turn) right away.

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.

examples.trans: I really dislike rainy days.
You hate waking up early in the morning, right?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나는 단 거 싫어하니까 시럽을 아예 넣지 말라 그랬지!
examples.trans: I hate sweet drinks, so I told you not to put any syrup in at all!
This expression comes from 'because I dislike'.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: Used as adverb (어쩌면).

examples.text: 한 시대를 풍미하는 스타라는 건 어쩌면 그 시대의 상징 같은 거 아닐까요?
examples.trans: Could a star who defines an era perhaps be a symbol of that entire time?
I thought it over again (perhaps).

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

meanings.note: Used as loanword noun (와이프).

examples.text: 예진아, 우리가 각자 다른 남자 여자 만나서 결혼을 한다 치자. 근데 서로의 와이프 남편이 우리의 이런 관계를 싫어해.
examples.trans: Ye-jin, suppose we each meet someone else and get married—and your husband and my wife dislike how close we are.
This point about wife is really important.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 1박 2일이랑 무슨 우정이 있다고 우정 출연을 하나, 깍듯한 선후배 사이지!
examples.trans: What friendship do I have with 2 Days & 1 Night to do an unpaid friendly cameo—we are strictly formal seniors and juniors!
Here the word for 'friendship' is key.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (유지할).

examples.text: 어쩌면 싫어하는 게 당연한 거 아닐까? 다른 사람이랑 결혼한 다음에도 어떻게 우리가 이런 관계를 유지할 수 있겠어?
examples.trans: Honestly, would disliking it not be completely natural? How could we keep up a bond like this after marrying other people?
Let us do that (maintain) right away.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (이사하면).

examples.text: 나 그동안 진짜 열심히 살았잖아. 이번에 이사하면 대학 때부터 해서 14번인가?
examples.trans: I really worked my tail off all these years—counting from college, does this move make fourteen times?

examples.text: 이제 나 이사하면 우리 제자리로 돌아가는 거다.
examples.trans: Once I move out into my place, the two of us go right back to where we belong.

meanings.note: Used as noun (이성).

examples.text: 싫으면 어쩔 건데? 이런 게 이성 간 우정의 한계 이런 거 아니겠냐!
examples.trans: Even if you hate it, what can you do? Is that not the natural limit of friendship between a man and a woman?
This point about opposite sex is really important.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as noun + directional (제자리로).

examples.text: 이제 나 이사하면 우리 제자리로 돌아가는 거다.
examples.trans: Once I move out into my place, the two of us go right back to where we belong.
This point about back to our proper place is really important.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to cause (trouble)
meanings.note: Used in idioms like 사고를 치다 (to cause trouble).

examples.trans: I caused trouble.
I caused trouble. (2)

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (한계가).

examples.text: 말 안 나게 조용히 찾는 데는 한계가 있고요, 신디가 평소에 친하게 지내던 사람도 없고…
examples.trans: There is a limit to searching quietly without word getting out, and Cindy has no close friends either…
This point about a limit is really important.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.
examples.trans: Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.
This expression comes from 'will regret'.
I waved my hand.
Please shake the bottle.
